questions.question: What are the tiny air sacs that make up the lungs called?
options: Bronchioles
Alveoli
Capillaries
Trachea

questions.question: Why are there millions of alveoli in human lungs instead of just one large sac?
options: To decrease the body temperature
To increase the surface area for gas exchange
To filter out dust and bacteria
To provide space for the heart

questions.question: How does the wall thickness of the alveoli help gas exchange occur quickly?
options: They are one cell thick to create a short diffusion distance
They are thick and muscular to pump gases
They have multiple layers to withstand pressure
They are elastic so they can expand

questions.question: Which substance is a key requirement for aerobic cellular respiration to take place?
options: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Ethanol
Oxygen

questions.question: Why do muscle cells typically contain a higher number of mitochondria than fat cells?
options: Muscle cells require more energy to do their work
Muscle cells store more food as glucose
Muscle cells need to produce more carbon dioxide
Muscle cells do not perform cellular respiration

questions.question: What are the products of anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms like yeast?
options: Lactic acid and water
Carbon dioxide and ethanol
Oxygen and glucose
Carbon dioxide and water

questions.question: What is another term used to describe anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms?
options: Photosynthesis
Fermentation
Combustive respiration
Aerobic synthesis

questions.question: Which product is built up in human muscles during anaerobic cellular respiration and can lead to cramps?
options: Ethanol
Glucose
Lactic acid
Carbon dioxide

questions.question: In which part of a cell does anaerobic cellular respiration take place?
options: Only in the mitochondria
Only in the cytoplasm
Inside the nucleus
Within the cell wall

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the energy release of anaerobic respiration to aerobic respiration?
options: Anaerobic respiration provides more energy and provides it more slowly
Anaerobic respiration provides less energy but provides it more quickly
Anaerobic respiration provides the same amount of energy but without using glucose
Anaerobic respiration provides more energy and provides it more quickly

questions.question: Which waste product of cellular respiration must be constantly removed from the body?
options: Oxygen
Glucose
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen

questions.question: During gas exchange in the lungs, how do oxygen and carbon dioxide move?
options: Both oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse into the blood
Oxygen diffuses from the lungs into the blood while carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the lungs
Oxygen diffuses from the blood into the lungs while carbon dioxide diffuses from the lungs into the blood
Both gases diffuse from the lungs into the air

questions.question: When does cellular respiration happen in living organisms?
options: Only when they are asleep
Only during physical exercise
All the time to provide energy to keep them alive
Only when they are eating food

questions.question: What is meant by the 'vital capacity' of the lungs?
options: The volume of air left in the lungs after a normal breath
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after inhaling fully
The rate at which oxygen enters the capillaries
The total amount of carbon dioxide produced in one minute

questions.question: In science, what does it mean if a measurement is said to be highly 'accurate'?
options: It is expressed to many decimal places
It is a rough estimate made without measuring
It is very close to the true value
It was measured using digital equipment

questions.question: How do the muscles in the chest move air out of the lungs during normal breathing?
options: The diaphragm contracts and the ribs move up and out
The diaphragm relaxes and the ribcage moves down and in
The lungs contract using their own muscular walls
The heart pumps air out of the chest cavity
